messages:
kevin: Heads-up — after the mesh egress policy rollout (r2026-03-18-3) several GPU-serving pods in eu-west1 cannot resolve external registries or reach our model storage. Pulls are timing out.

maya: saw it too, started ~10:15 UTC. DNS lookups from the sidecar fail (/etc/resolv.conf looks fine). Pod-level curl to 1.1.1.1 times out.

samir: envoy logs show repeated CONNECT failed / upstream reset for outbound: CONNECT cluster_registry:443. Also spikes in 5xx on the egress gateway.

julia: suspect egress policy is too strict — we accidentally locked down UDP/TCP 53 or the DNAT passthrough for node-local DNS. Did the rollout change the mesh.egress.allowlist rules?

ashley: yes, the policy removed the legacy passthrough for kube-dns to force flows through egress-gw. That created a DNAT -> gateway path but the gateway's SNAT pool is exhausted on some nodepools (we're seeing TCP ephemeral port exhaustion).

kevin: can we do a quick mitigation? Need model pulls back for canary traffic. @oncall-bot can you escalate if we need infra blip?

ops-bot: Incident created: INC-2026-042 (egress-sidecar-dns). Pager duty notified.

dena: temporary mitigation suggestion: allow UDP/TCP 53 to bypass sidecar/egress gateway for node-local DNS. Quick kubectl patch to the egress policy should be low-risk. Example: 

```
apiVersion: networking.redwood/v1
kind: EgressPolicy
metadata:
  name: allow-node-dns-bypass
spec:
  patch: allow
  rules:
    - destination: 0.0.0.0/0
      ports: [53/udp, 53/tcp]
      action: BYPASS_EGRESS_GATEWAY
  target: node-local-dns
```

(deploy the patch in eu-west1 only as a canary).

maya: applied similar patch to the eu-west1 staging pool. Confirming: pods that previously failed can now resolve external hosts and model pulls moving again.

samir: still seeing some 502s from the gateway when traffic levels spike — probably the SNAT pool exhaustion / connection tracking. We should also increase the gateway NAT port pool or enable per-node SNAT for heavy-serving nodepools.

julia: agreed. Follow-up items: (1) revert the overly-restrictive default passthrough removal, (2) add a test to the rollout job that hits external DNS and model registry endpoints before promoting a policy, (3) capacity bump on egress-gw NAT for eu-west1.

ashley: cost note — increasing NAT capacity (more gateway VMs) will add ~€0.8k/week for eu-west1 peak; per-request cost may go down if we restore node-local SNAT and avoid gateway hops for internal traffic. We should include an ops cost estimate in the RFC.

kevin: logging this as a postmortem candidate. I'll open a short incident write-up with timeline and mitigation steps. Please add command snippets, config diffs, and any missing logs to the incident.

maya: quick question — are there any known interactions with the healthchecks on our internal load balancers when bypassing the egress-gw? Need to ensure LB healthchecks still route correctly.

samir: healthchecks are fine as long as we don't change the source IP expectations. If we enable BYPASS_EGRESS_GATEWAY for node-local-dns only, LBs unaffected. If we revert to node-local SNAT for model pulls, LBs might see different source IPs; add a test.

dena: postmortem action items I'll add to the incident: gating rollout with e2e external resolution check, add SNAT pool autoscaling, and document the allowed DNS bypass exception in the mesh policy guide (link: https://docs.redwood.internal/infra/egress-policies).

kevin: thanks all. For now eu-west1 looks stable after the bypass patch. I'll schedule the RFC for the long-term rollback + NAT autoscale tomorrow. :thumbsup:
